steps.name: Library sizes and count-scale characterization
caveats: Salmon output 'as delivered' may be length-scaled (fractional values) even when called counts — the profile does not say; inspect the values, do not assume integers.
A ~4x-shallow sample implies ratio_to_median ~0.25; confirm the direction and magnitude from the data.
Gene names arrive in whatever namespace Salmon used; carry them forward unchanged — no ID mapping is needed for QC.
steps.context: Data: /eval-four-models-v2-without-qc-only-n6-s1-1/data/inputs/counts/counts.csv (12000 x 13 CSV; gene-level Salmon output as delivered, 12 samples plus one gene-name column) and /eval-four-models-v2-without-qc-only-n6-s1-1/data/inputs/metadata/metadata.csv (12 x 2: sample, condition = atopic dermatitis lesional vs control, 6+6, unpaired, single batch). Known caveat: sample_01 has a library size about 4x below the median. No prior QC was run on this dataset (it was delivered without QC), so this step is the first depth check.
steps.question: What is the per-sample library size of the 12 skin samples (6 atopic dermatitis lesional vs 6 control), and is the delivered Salmon matrix raw counts or length-corrected — the fact that decides the normalization used by the downstream PCA and distance steps?
constraints: Join samples by exact name between counts.csv columns and metadata.csv rows; verify 12/12 match and report any mismatch explicitly rather than dropping silently.
Do not run differential expression or any downstream biology in this step.
Persist the normalized matrix and the scale-classification decision (with evidence) to a step output that T1S2 and T1S3 reuse without re-deriving.
Report the actual measured ratio_to_median for sample_01 — do not assume 0.25.
steps.description: Load counts.csv and metadata.csv; identify the gene-name column and the 12 sample columns. Join to metadata by exact sample name. Compute per-sample library size (column sum) and ratio to the median library size. Characterize the count scale: fraction of integer-valued entries and log10 median of nonzero entries, to classify the matrix as raw counts (integers, totals in the 1e6-1e7 range) or length-scaled/TPM-like (fractional, O(1) or less). Then build the single normalized matrix all later steps consume: log2(CPM+1) if raw counts, log2(TPM+1) if TPM-like — and record which branch was taken and why. Produce a depth bar chart of the 12 library sizes colored by condition with the median line.
acceptance_criteria: library_sizes.tsv with 12 rows: sample, condition, total_counts, ratio_to_median.
Explicit scale classification (raw counts vs length-scaled) backed by the integer-fraction and magnitude evidence, recorded in the step output.
Normalized expression matrix (12000 x 12) saved, with the normalization rule documented in the output.
Depth bar chart (12 samples, colored by condition, median line, sample_01 annotated).

steps.name: PCA of the 12 samples
caveats: n=12 (6 per arm): one point can visibly move a component axis — note if a component is dominated by a single sample, especially sample_01.
PCA on log-normalized bulk counts is standard for QC visualization; it is not a statistical test of group separation — do not attach p-values here.
steps.context: Consumes the normalized matrix and the scale-classification decision from T1S1. Conditions: atopic dermatitis lesional (n=6) vs control (n=6). sample_01 is the pre-flagged low-depth sample; its PC position is a deliverable, not a post-hoc finding.
steps.question: In principal components, do atopic dermatitis lesional and control skin samples form distinct patterns, and does sample_01 (the shallow sample) load as an outlier along any major component?
constraints: Use the T1S1 normalized matrix exactly as produced — do not re-normalize or re-filter genes here.
This is a QC view, not a clustering claim: do not describe PC groupings as clusters or biological subtypes.
steps.description: Run PCA (SVD / prcomp equivalent) on the T1S1 normalized matrix, genes as variables. Report percent variance explained for PC1-PC3. Produce PC1-PC2 (and PC1-PC3 if it adds information) scatter plots: points colored by condition (lesional vs control), labeled by sample name, sample_01 highlighted. Compute each sample's distance from the centroid in PC space (leverage) and report it alongside the condition labels. State plainly whether the conditions separate on PC1/PC2 and exactly where sample_01 sits.
acceptance_criteria: pca.png: PC1-PC2 scatter, colored by condition, all 12 samples labeled, sample_01 highlighted.
pca_coordinates.csv: 12 rows with PC1-PC3 scores and PC-space distance from centroid.
Percent variance explained for PC1-PC3 reported.
Explicit statement: (a) whether lesional vs control is visible on PC1/PC2, (b) sample_01's PC position relative to the other 11.

steps.name: Sample-to-sample distances and hierarchical clustering
caveats: With 12 points, dendrogram topology is metric-sensitive — that is why both metrics are reported; do not narrate one topology as 'the' structure.
A shallow sample tends to be noisier, which can inflate its distance to all others — this is evidence for T1S4's rule, not a verdict by itself.
steps.context: Consumes the same normalized matrix from T1S1. Conditions: atopic dermatitis lesional (n=6) vs control (n=6), single batch, unpaired. sample_01 is the pre-flagged low-depth sample; its rank in sample-to-sample distance is a deliverable.
steps.question: What are the pairwise distances among the 12 samples, and does the dendrogram place sample_01 outside the condition-consistent structure?
constraints: Use the T1S1 normalized matrix exactly as produced.
Report both metrics side by side; do not silently choose one as 'the' distance.
steps.description: Compute the 12x12 pairwise sample distance on the T1S1 normalized matrix under two metrics: 1 - Pearson correlation and Euclidean. Produce a distance heatmap (samples on both axes, annotated by condition) and a hierarchical-clustering dendrogram (average linkage) per metric, branches annotated by condition. Compute each sample's mean distance to the other 11 under both metrics, rank all 12, and report sample_01's rank and whether it is top-2 under either metric.
acceptance_criteria: distance_heatmap.png (12x12, both metrics or one panel each), dendrogram.png(s) with condition annotations.
sample_distances.tsv: per sample, mean distance to the other 11 and rank under 1-Pearson and Euclidean.
Explicit statement of whether sample_01 is top-2 in mean distance under either metric.

steps.name: Verdict on sample_01 (shallow library)
caveats: Depth alone is not grounds for exclusion: CPM/median-ratio style normalization is robust to library size, so a shallow but otherwise typical sample should be retained with a caveat — let the outlier flags drive the call.
With 6 per arm, any exclusion materially changes the design; the verdict should name that cost, not just the quality benefit.
If the numbers sit exactly on a rule boundary (e.g., ratio 0.5, tied distance rank), say so and present both readings rather than forcing one.
steps.context: Integrates only the outputs of T1S1 (library_sizes.tsv, sample_01 ratio_to_median), T1S2 (PC leverage), and T1S3 (distance ranks). Read sample_01's condition from metadata.csv (condition: atopic dermatitis lesional vs control) to state the effect on arm balance. The dataset went in without QC, so this verdict is the QC gate for everything downstream.
steps.question: Given its library size, its PC position, and its sample-to-sample distances, should sample_01 be excluded or retained for the downstream atopic dermatitis lesional vs control test?
constraints: Do not introduce any new statistic or test in this step — integrate only T1S1-T1S3 outputs.
The recommendation must state the tradeoff explicitly: exclusion removes one of six samples in its arm, unbalancing the 6 vs 6 design.
Do not re-run PCA, distances, or library-size computations here.
steps.description: Apply a pre-registered rule to the actual numbers: (a) depth flag — shallow if ratio_to_median < 0.5; (b) outlier flag — top-2 mean sample distance under either metric, or top-2 PC leverage. Decision: shallow AND outlier -> recommend exclusion from downstream testing, report to user; shallow but not an outlier -> retain with an explicit low-depth caveat (reduced per-gene sensitivity in that sample); not shallow -> retain. State the arm-balance consequence of exclusion (e.g., 5 vs 6 if sample_01 is lesional or control) and the power implication in one sentence. Write the verdict as a short report: the rule, the triggering numbers from T1S1-T1S3, and the recommendation.
acceptance_criteria: verdict.md containing: sample_01's condition, its ratio_to_median, its distance rank(s), its PC leverage, the rule applied, and a single unambiguous retain/exclude recommendation with reasoning.
Explicit arm-balance statement (e.g., 'excluding sample_01 leaves 5 lesional vs 6 control') and a one-sentence power implication.
No new statistical results beyond what T1S1-T1S3 computed.

plan.title: AD skin RNA-seq pre-DE sample QC and depth verdict
plan.analytical_narrative: The research question is explicitly pre-hypothesis-testing: how do the twelve samples look before any atopic dermatitis lesional vs control test is run. The plan therefore produces only QC diagnostics — no differential expression, no enrichment, no references. T1S1 runs first because the delivered Salmon matrix's length-correction status is not recorded in the profile (12000 x 13 gene-level counts as delivered); classifying the count scale (raw integer counts vs length-scaled/TPM-like) determines the correct normalization (log2 CPM vs log2 TPM+1) and T1S1 carries that decision forward. T1S2 (PCA) and T1S3 (pairwise distances + hclust) then run in parallel on the same normalized matrix, both examining whether the known ~4x-shallow sample_01 sits apart from the 6-vs-6 condition structure. T1S4 integrates the three outputs with a pre-registered rule to deliver the requested verdict on sample_01, including the arm-balance cost (5 vs 6) of exclusion. No reference data from /mnt/refs is needed for QC; the human WikiPathways/UniProt files are irrelevant here.
